citation.title: A real-time velocity diagnostic for NSTX
citation.authors: M. Podestà and R. E. Bell

topic: Real-time carbon CHERS toroidal-velocity diagnostic interfaced to the NSTX plasma control system
own_question: How can C VI charge-exchange spectroscopy be redesigned to supply toroidal velocity to the plasma control system at kHz rates?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper describes the hardware and software design: added fibers per channel, no slit or chopper, Cascade CCDs up to 5 kHz, and a C++ Levenberg-Marquardt two-gaussian fit reported at 120 μs or less for up to 8 channels. Output goes to the plasma control system through an analog card. Evidence is limited to neon-glow wavelength scatter and a reanalysis of existing CHERS plasma data. There was no NB-plasma operation of RTV, and the ion-temperature range is limited (about 300 eV or more is inferable), with velocity as the primary output.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Fast spectroscopic impurity-velocity measurement has been engineered for real-time control on NSTX, trading spectral resolution and temperature capability for photon throughput and speed.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.2 Sec. II; p.3 Sec. II.C; Table I
claim_checks.qualification: Carbon impurity velocity on NSTX, not KSTAR temperature. Design stage only; first plasma operation was still planned.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: A simplified real-time spectral fit has been reported to track offline CHERS velocity evolution, with sub-millisecond computation.
claim_checks.qualification: Agreement is stated in the text and not quantified; the figure was not viewed. The 120 μs figure is the authors' computing time, not a control loop demonstrated in a plasma.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The inputs are current-frame spectra, and the output is the current-frame velocity (an upstream spectrum reader, not a temporal nowcast). The 100 μs value is the stated minimum latency from exposure to readout end. Report arrival in the plasma control system is not measured beyond a polling interval of 200 μs.
validation_if_relevant: Wavelength standard deviation over 100 frames in neon glow. Offline reanalysis of a single discharge. No held-out set and no feedback demonstration.
forbidden_inferences: RTV measured temperature in real time
applies to KSTAR or main-ion Ti
faster upstream reading removes or guarantees need for nowcasting
all prior CES work is noncausal
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Use as a concrete precedent for the upstream route of faster CES acquisition and fitting. It contrasts with our downstream estimation of the current report before it is available. Cite cautiously as a design and early-test paper.
